title.text: Observe: one toolbar, one timeline, one time picker

fix.text:
What changes, by your four points:
1. One aligned toolbar row: SQL bar (plain text = name/trace-id match), zoom −/+, reset, time picker, Live. The separate search box, SORT and duration rows go: sort lives in column headers, duration is a facet + SQL.
2. Time picker button opens presets (5m → 30d) with custom range inside it.
3. Zooming shows a 'Zoomed … ✕' chip and the ↺ button returns to the preset you came from.
4. The from/to row you saw is the absolute-range editor that appears after a zoom; it moves into the picker.
Revision 2: amber removed from charts (lime is the secondary series; amber stays only on the WARN label). Traces lead with three linked charts: spans/min, errors, duration p50/p95.

title2.text: Home and Card pages: each kind leads with what it is, then how it is behaving

cardsfix.text:
Card pages, shared shape:
• Header: name, kind, version, status, one-line description; uid shortened with copy.
• Kind-specific hero: Agent = composition graph, Prompt = the messages, Model = interface + artifacts.
• Vitals strip from Bifrost, filtered to this component's spans (agent.invoke / prompt.render / model.predict).
• Verification table: the Verifiers bound to it, with trend and latest.
• Right rail: relationships with kind pills, compact metadata.
• Tabs: Overview · Versions · YAML (raw).
Gone: one box per spec field, "Declared empty." boxes, full hashes, "read-only projection of server truth".

title3.text: Query: explore the warehouse in SQL — table, chart, details, history

querynote.text:
Query (extends foundation Q-01):
• Same toolbar row: time range applies to each table's time column; limit; Copy SQL; CSV; Run ⌘↵ / Cancel.
• Catalog of real vala tables; correlation columns (card_uid, run_id) highlighted — they join any table.
• Starter queries show the joins (spans ⋈ verification.results on run_id).
• Results: Table · Chart (line/bar/area/number, x/y/group from result columns) · Details (query id, status, time, rows, bytes, error) · History.
• card_uid values render as their Card.
• Bounds shown are Oracle's real ones: one read-only SELECT, SQL ≤ 64 KiB, 2 h default deadline; the page's Limit bounds rows.

title4.text: Verify: overview of results → click one → the result

verifynote.text:
Revision 11 — one generic Verifier (verifier-building-blocks). There is no Eval, Task or Drift kind: a Verifier has inputs, optional steps (extract · agent · code), requirements (assert · trace · agent · code · drift checks) and a decide rule (all | pass_rate).

Overview: one row per vala.verification.results row (one execution). Columns: Verifier, subject · Service, run (or window), requirement summary, verdict. Facets: verdict, Verifier, failed requirement, Service, subject, run. Group by: Verifier / requirement / Service / run.

Result: one page for every Verifier. Requirements in declaration order with outcome (passed · failed · inconclusive · not_applicable), reason, actual, citations and check provenance; steps with action, timing, attempts and tool calls; pinned evidence; provenance (execution, binding, sub/act principals, on_failure dispatches); this Verifier's pass rate by requirement / subject / run.

Window result: the same page when the Verifier judges samples on a schedule. A drift requirement expands to its features (vala.drift.result_features, joined on result_id + requirement_id), history across windows and distribution vs baseline. No manual run: window Verifiers refuse verify().

Stored sources: vala.verification.results (verdict, execution_status, verifier_card_uid, card_uid = subject, owner_card_uid, binding_id, run_id, window_start/end, outcome). outcome is a sensitive Variant: requirement and step detail needs the elevated payload permission; without it rows show verdict only.
